races.name: Ladbrokes 'Bet £5 Get £30 New Customer Offer' EBF Maiden Fillies' Stakes (GBB Race)

runners_data.name: Ashina
runners_data.note: Hold-up filly for O'Meara and Tudhope who finished sixth on debut over 6f Good; the step from 5f back to 6f suits but she'll need a stronger pace than this race is likely to generate to land her finishing effort.

runners_data.name: Dadawada
runners_data.note: Pressed from a prominent position when fifth over 5f Good for Kellett and Eaves; the step up to 6f is a mild query but her natural racing position puts her ideally placed to make use of the controlled fractions.

runners_data.name: Desert Smoke
runners_data.note: Hold-up mare for Hugo Palmer who has two moderate finishes on Good ground at 6f; Paul Mulrennan will have to produce her from off the pace, which is a structural disadvantage in a race likely to be run at a measured tempo.

runners_data.name: Fly Smartly
runners_data.note: Has a placed effort (third over 5f Good) to her name and races prominently, making her a natural beneficiary of the expected pace map; De Aguiar's yard is lightly raced but Donagh O'Connor is an able handler and this extra furlong may sharpen her chance.

runners_data.name: Lady Titania
runners_data.note: Wore a tongue-tie when beaten seventh on debut over 6f Good for K.R. Burke; races prominently and Burke's yard is in decent form at T14 8/46, but the debut run was modest and she needs significant improvement.

runners_data.name: La Flor Granada
runners_data.note: Debut runner for Fahey with no public form lines; her running style is unknown, making her a pure wildcard, though Fahey regularly produces well-schooled first-timers and Oisin Orr is a sharp tactical rider who will position her appropriately.

runners_data.name: Myesme
runners_data.note: First-time starter for Edward Bethell with unknown style; Bethell's yard is running at a respectable 7/29 over 14 days, and Jason Hart is an experienced pilot, but without form there is no structural anchor for where she will fit into this race.

runners_data.name: Next Of Kin
runners_data.note: Showed ability with a debut third over 6f Good for Haggas and Cieren Fallon, the most informative piece of form in this field; her running style is uncharted but Haggas debutants who place first time out often improve sharply, and the Good Ayr surface repeats exactly her last outing.

runners_data.name: Oh So Slow Sloth
runners_data.note: Finished sixth on debut but maps as the clear front-runner here; a [STYLE_FIT] flag applies because this is effectively a different task — dictating from the front after racing more passively before — and Rebecca Menzies' yard is out of form at T14 0/11, which tempers confidence despite the positional advantage.

races.paceDynamic: Oh So Slow Sloth is the sole confirmed front-runner in this nine-runner maiden, and with Dadawada, Fly Smartly, and Lady Titania likely to press for prominent positions, the early order will involve some jostling before Oh So Slow Sloth settles into an uncontested lead. Once Oh So Slow Sloth establishes at the front, the pace should be honest but controlled — a lone leader on Good ground over 6f at Ayr typically sets a rhythm that neither collapses nor scorches, giving the field a genuine target to aim at from halfway. The hold-up horses — Ashina, Desert Smoke, and Next Of Kin — will need to cover ground in the straight, but the uncontested nature of the lead means the pace is unlikely to be strong enough to guarantee they are finishing faster than the race is being run. This race shape most clearly favours horses that can race prominently or within a length or two of the pace, tracking Oh So Slow Sloth before asserting in the final furlong, rather than those forced to make up ground from the back.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Lone Leader Controls
scenarios.trigger: If Oh So Slow Sloth is allowed to stride clear unchallenged and the prominent trio settle just off rather than pressing hard.
scenarios.body: Oh So Slow Sloth sets a controlled, sustainable tempo that bleeds the field of zip, with the race unfolding in a single file and the leader tough to peg back; Dadawada and Fly Smartly, sitting closest to the pace, are best placed to challenge if the leader does tire in the final 100 yards.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Horses Dominate
scenarios.trigger: If Dadawada or Fly Smartly tracks Oh So Slow Sloth closely enough to pounce early in the straight before the leader can accelerate.
scenarios.body: A compact, prominent-led finish plays out with one of the chasing prominent types wearing down Oh So Slow Sloth from the 2f pole; Fly Smartly's placed form over 5f and Dadawada's recent 5f experience both suggest enough natural pace to make this a credible shape.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Late Closers Pounce
scenarios.trigger: If the early pace proves genuinely strong and the front runners tie each other up, opening a gap for hold-up horses to reel them in.
scenarios.body: Ashina or Desert Smoke, settled in the rear, would need Oh So Slow Sloth and the prominent pair to race at an unsustainably strong clip to find clear daylight in the final furlong; this is structurally less likely given the sole front-runner dynamic, but Next Of Kin's debutant profile and Haggas's record make this worth a small slice.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Debutant Upsets
scenarios.trigger: If one of the unexposed newcomers — La Flor Granada or Myesme — arrives with significant home reputation and displays a natural prominent or pace-tracking style that was unknown before the off.
scenarios.body: Fahey and Bethell both have the tools to produce a well-schooled first-time runner that settles in behind the pace and produces a sharp turn of foot on Good ground; without form lines to anchor them, these two remain speculative but cannot be wholly dismissed in a field where no runner has an ORR above 0.

watchPoints.text: Oh So Slow Sloth's trainer Rebecca Menzies is running at 0 wins from 11 over the last 14 days — if the filly is below her best the entire race shape collapses, as no other horse here has confirmed front-running ability.

Next Of Kin (Haggas/Fallon) is the most interesting form entry: a debut third over the identical 6f Good trip, and Haggas's record of improving second-time runners means she could be significantly better than her form string suggests — watch the market.

La Flor Granada and Myesme are both unexposed debutants from capable yards (Fahey and Bethell); if either shows early pace and slots into a prominent position, the race shape changes materially from what the confirmed data suggests.

Fly Smartly steps up from 5f to 6f, a trip she hasn't yet been tried over — this extra furlong is the key unknown for a horse that has only shown her pace over shorter, and how she handles the distance will determine whether her prominent position converts into a finish.

races.name: 'Ladbrokes Get More With Racing Bet Builder' Classified Stakes

runners_data.name: Charcon
runners_data.note: Lightly raced 3yo with Ben Haslam; 16 days since last run, headgear on, but true inclination is to race from the rear — the crowded hold-up division means she will likely settle in midfield rather than her preferred position, which tempers her winning chance in a race likely to be run at a controlled gallop.
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last five starts, Charcon has at least shown experience over today's trip and conditions, and 16 days between runs suggests she arrives fresh; a rating of 52 gives her a slight edge over her official mark, though consecutive moderate finishes make a big run hard to envisage.

runners_data.name: Hawksworth
runners_data.note: Three runs only for Quinn yard, returning from 45 days off; form figures of 7-5-0 suggest limited progression, and while Good ground is fine, stepping up to a mile without winning evidence over that trip adds doubt alongside the redistribution away from a true rear position.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last three starts, with unplaced efforts his most recent form, Hawksworth is hard to fancy on these figures — ranked last of the 12 — though he has run over today's trip before and stall two could be a neutral factor.

runners_data.name: Royal Baroness
runners_data.note: Trainer R Mike Smith runs one at a time and this filly returns after 66 days, which is notable; she has placed twice at 8f on Good-family going (her best sim-going record), and though she gravitates toward hold-up tactics naturally, in a depleted pace scenario she could find herself in a more forward position than usual — a quiet each-way angle.
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last five starts and returning after 66 days off, Royal Baroness faces a stiff ask from stall five carrying 128 lb — though she has run over today's distance and going before, and a third last time out offers a sliver of encouragement.

runners_data.name: Sanny Doo
runners_data.note: Jim Goldie runner, just two days since last outing which is extremely quick turnaround; form string of 886770 tells a blunt story and, despite being placed in midfield on the map, her natural inclination is further back — the short recovery combined with modest form makes it hard to raise confidence here.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last six starts and ranked 11 of 12 on our figures, Sanny Doo has shown little encouragement in recent outings, and a trainer striking at just 4% over the past fortnight adds to concerns — experience over today's trip and going is about the best that can be said.

runners_data.name: Hostelry
runners_data.note: Ruth Carr's 9yo veteran returns just nine days after her last run wearing a visor; her record of 455545 over 8-9f on Good is remarkably consistent, she has won and placed multiple times in similar going, and her T14 strike-rate of 5/25 is the most active in the field — a hold-up type who genuinely stays and finds form fresh.
runners_data.comment: Hostelry has run over today's trip and going, rates 9 lb clear of her mark on our figures, and at just nine days since her last start she arrives in peak freshness — the risk is she's been winless in her last six starts, suggesting she finds ways to be denied.

runners_data.name: Millbuie
runners_data.note: The lone confirmed front-runner for Ewan Whillans, she wears tongue-tie and has shown the ability to place from the front (2nd at 10f Standout); with no rivals likely to challenge her for the lead, she can set whatever tempo suits her on Good over this mile — the key horse for shaping the entire race.
runners_data.comment: Millbuie arrives on a tight 10-day turnaround carrying 135 lb from stall four, and his third three starts back and runner-up last time out show he's capable of mixing it at this level, with experience over today's trip and going an added plus; the risk is that he's yet to win in recent starts.

runners_data.name: Ring Of Gold
runners_data.note: Michael & David Easterby 9yo, consistent profile of mid-to-high single finishes, visor worn; Good going is fine but sim-going record shows 0W0P in 15 relevant starts, and true hold-up style redistributed into midfield means he is unlikely to strike from a suboptimal berth in a race unlikely to collapse for closers.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last six starts, Ring Of Gold has consecutive seventh-placed finishes to overcome, though he has run over today's trip and going before and a rating of 51 offers some encouragement; the 135 lb burden and draw 11 are notable factors as he returns just nine days later.

runners_data.name: Spirit Of Nature
runners_data.note: Jim Goldie's second runner, 14 days since last run, no headgear; his 4th and 3rd over 8-11f on Good shows he handles the surface and his best efforts have come when tracking leaders — if he can secure a forward midfield pitch in a race with only one genuine pace-setter, he represents a live threat.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last four starts — seventh last time out and fourth three starts back, with a third four starts back offering a flicker of hope — Spirit Of Nature faces an uphill task here, with a trainer badly out of form (4%) and 135 lb to carry from stall seven adding further weight to the concerns.

runners_data.name: Bridgefoot Rambler
runners_data.note: Blinkered 4yo for Stephen Hanlon, 25 days off; three of his last five runs have been at 8f on Good and his 3rd most recently (Goodwood, 8f Good) shows he can place — naturally a hold-up type squeezed toward midfield by the congested rearguard, which does limit his chance if the gallop doesn't genuinely stretch the field.
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last five starts and ranked tenth of twelve on our figures, Bridgefoot Rambler faces a stiff ask, though a third last time out offers a crumb of encouragement and she has run over today's trip and going before.

runners_data.name: Concert Boy
runners_data.note: Katie Scott's 6yo wears blinkers; form of 640870 is uninspiring with a zero (non-completion) recently, and while 8f on Good is within his comfort zone, sim-going record shows 0W0P in 15 comparable runs — hard to see where the improvement comes from at OR 50.
runners_data.comment: Ranked top of the 12 runners on our ratings, Concert Boy has run over today's trip and going before and returns fit on 20 days' rest carrying 135 lb from stall 3; the concern is that he's been winless in his last six starts, including two unplaced efforts.

runners_data.name: Due Respect
runners_data.note: Gary Rutherford's 4yo, just six days since last run, wearing a visor; impressively consistent on Good ground over 6-7f (all five recent runs on Good), but stepping up to a mile here for the first time in recent form is a genuine query — the pace redistribution away from his natural position adds another layer of doubt, and his style_fit score of 0.93 is the highest in the field.
runners_data.comment: Yet to win in her last six starts, Due Respect does at least have experience over today's trip and going, and a fifth last time out keeps her in reasonable nick; however, winless recent form and a testing 135 lb from stall 12 make progress hard to envisage.

runners_data.name: Game Management
runners_data.note: Lizzie Quinlan's 5yo returns from an extraordinary 314-day absence; has won and placed on Good ground but those results came over 17f (a totally different sphere), and his only form over 8-9f comes on Soft — the layoff combined with the going uncertainty makes him a significant unknown quantity on race day.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last four starts and off the track for 314 days, Game Management faces a stiff return, yet he has run over today's distance and going before and our figures suggest he holds more ability than his official mark of 50 implies.

races.paceDynamic: Millbuie is the sole confirmed front-runner in this 12-runner field and, with no genuine rival likely to push for the lead from the outside, she can dictate a sustainable, unhurried gallop from the front on Good ground over a mile at Ayr. With only one horse setting a controlled pace, the tempo is likely to be modest early before quickening in the home straight, which classically rewards those sitting close to or just off the pace who can travel economically and pounce. This race shape strongly favours prominent racers and those sitting just behind the leader — horses who can track the single pace-setter and produce a clean, uncomplicated challenge in the straight without needing to make up excessive ground. The field holds considerably more hold-up types than can genuinely fill rear positions, with Bridgefoot Rambler, Due Respect, Charcon, Royal Baroness, Ring Of Gold, Hawksworth and Sanny Doo all redistributed to midfield on the map — Millbuie, and any runner prepared to race prominently from the outset, are most likely to secure the natural positions that suit.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Millbuie Controls, Stays On
scenarios.trigger: If Millbuie leads unchallenged and dictates a moderate gallop that becomes a stamina-test in the final two furlongs.
scenarios.body: Millbuie sets a comfortable tempo, the field strings out behind her, and those without the class or condition to sustain a run from deep find the winner already gone; horses racing close to her wheel benefit most from minimal ground-loss and a well-timed challenge.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Pair Pounce Late
scenarios.trigger: If a horse tracks Millbuie in second or third and produces a decisive kick in the closing stages as her pace inevitably slows.
scenarios.body: A single moderate pace collapses in the final furlong once challengers commit, and a horse with enough tactical speed to sit just off the leader then pick up cleanly will have the race won before closers can close; Hostelry's consistent form at 8-9f on Good suits this perfectly.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Closers Grind Through
scenarios.trigger: If Millbuie sets a genuinely strong early pace and the field is strung out, allowing a hold-up horse to arrive late with untapped reserves.
scenarios.body: This scenario requires the pace to be surprisingly strong for a lone front-runner in a modest classified stakes, which is low probability given Millbuie's relaxed racing style; if it materialises, a true hold-up type with class over the trip would benefit, but most of the genuine closers here have been redistributed from their natural position and their form over 8f on Good is limited.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Chaos, No True Gallop
scenarios.trigger: If the early pace is so pedestrian it collapses into a sprint finish over the final two furlongs with the whole field compressed.
scenarios.body: A falsely-run race would make finishing position largely down to jockey positioning and sprint speed, disadvantaging horses lacking tactical pace and favouring those with the highest top-speed ratings who can quicken sharply; in this OR-banded classified stakes, few runners have demonstrated the raw acceleration this scenario demands.

watchPoints.text: Millbuie controls the entire race tempo — if she finds a comfortable solo lead and is allowed to bowl along at a moderate clip, her rivals will be playing catch-up on her terms; any significant market move for her warrants attention.

Spirit Of Nature and Hostelry are the two hold-up types with genuine sim-going form at this distance who could legitimately secure a mid-pack tracking position — watch their pre-race positioning and early running, as either grabbing second or third early would put them in the ideal scenario.

Due Respect's step up to a mile is the most significant unknown in the field — he has run all five recent starts over 6-7f on Good and looked quick, but there is no evidence he stays a mile, and if the pace is slow he may find himself up with the pace before fading.

Game Management's 314-day absence is unprecedented in this field — trainer Lizzie Quinlan's T14 record of 0/5 offers no confidence in an immediate return to form, and backers should be aware he is essentially an unknown quantity returning from nearly a year off.

The Jim Goldie yard has two runners (Sanny Doo and Spirit Of Nature) — Sanny Doo ran just two days ago which is unusually quick, and the stable's T14 rate of 2/51 is modest; watch whether there is any market divergence between the pair suggesting stable confidence lies with one over the other.

races.name: Ladbrokes 'Big Daily Boosts On Racing' Handicap Stakes

runners_data.name: Keep Me Stable
runners_data.note: Genuine prominent runner who is best placed tactically in this race, sitting second behind Kelpie Grey; Linda Perratt's yard is in excellent form at T14 5/13, and three days since last run is tight but recent form shows a return to 7f good ground suits, having placed twice at this trip in similar conditions.
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last five starts and ranked near the foot of our figures, Keep Me Stable faces a stiff task here; second last time out offers some encouragement, but three days between runs and 135 lb make her hard to fancy.

runners_data.name: Carmel Valley
runners_data.note: Three-year-old hold-up type for Katie Scott and Jason Hart who has placed twice recently including a second over 8f on good; the step back to 7f on good ground is within their range based on form figures, and drawing on fresh legs at 14 days should help, though a mid-pack position leaves them dependent on a proper run of racing room.
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last five starts, Carmel Valley nevertheless shows consistency with a second and a third in recent outings; she has run over today's trip and going before, but carrying 134 lb from stall seven, a step up in class on her official mark of 63 makes the task demanding.

runners_data.name: Black Rock Beauty
runners_data.note: Won over 7f on good at this track last time for Fahey, which is a compelling course-and-distance angle; however their natural style is hold-up racing, and with so many hold-up types in this field they are unlikely to get a true back-of-the-field position — racing closer than ideal may not suit their finishing kick, with headgear (p) suggesting connections want them sharper early.
runners_data.comment: Black Rock Beauty won three starts back but has since finished sixth and third in recent starts, so his consistency is a question mark; he has run over today's trip and going, carries 134 lb from stall six, and a rating of 62 leaves him with plenty to find on the pick of these.

runners_data.name: Albeyours
runners_data.note: Hollinshead's hold-up performer won over 7f on soft last time out and has shown a liking for give in the ground previously; they are a true sit-and-wait type who ideally needs a strong pace to close into, and with Kelpie Grey likely to control things at a measured tempo, their prospects depend on the race quickening more than expected in the final stages.
runners_data.comment: Albeyours has won once in her last five starts, with a seventh last time out doing little to inspire confidence, and ranked 12 of 13 on our figures she faces a stiff task here; experience over today's trip and going at least means conditions aren't new to her.

runners_data.name: Joshuas Dream
runners_data.note: Recent form figures of 9-12-8-17 make grim reading, and while they have placed once in five recent runs, the form over 5-6f on varied going gives limited confidence stepping up in company over 7f on good at Ayr; their natural rear-of-field style is compromised by the traffic of other hold-up types.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last four starts, with two unplaced efforts among them, Joshuas Dream is ranked bottom of these on our figures and his trainer is badly out of form at 4% over the past fortnight — at least he has run over today's trip and going before, and 14 days between runs suggests he's ready.

runners_data.name: Novak
runners_data.note: Seven-year-old hold-up type for Iain Jardine who has been consistent without winning, placing four times from six recent runs including a second over 7f on good; Andrew Mullen takes over in the saddle and the yard is active at T14 6/30, but getting a clear run from a true hold-up position in a field this large is the key obstacle.
runners_data.comment: Novak arrives here winless in his last six starts, though a third three starts back and a second four starts back hint at some ability; yet back-to-back fourths most recently suggest he finds winning hard to come by, and 138 lb from stall 11 adds no favours.

runners_data.name: Stoneywell
runners_data.note: Form figures of 8-7-7-9-8 tell a story of consistent mid-to-rear finishes without threatening, and 52 days off the track adds a layer of doubt about match sharpness; Hollinshead sends out another hold-up type into an already congested rear section, and headgear (b) suggests they need a trigger the race shape may not provide.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last five starts, with a sequence of mid-to-rear finishes, Stoneywell is hard to fancy at the weights carrying 137 lb from stall 8; he has run over today's trip and going before, but our figures rank him tenth of thirteen.

runners_data.name: Tropez Power
runners_data.note: Headgear (v) indicates a horse that can switch off, and Mark Walford's veteran has been placed once in five recent runs but form figures of 9-8-8-6-6 do not inspire confidence over 7f on good; 14 days since last run is fine, but getting competitive from their natural position at the back of a strong-paced 13-runner field looks difficult.
runners_data.comment: Tropez Power has run over today's trip and going and our rating of 67 puts him ahead of his official mark, suggesting he's better than his recent winless sequence implies; the risk is that his last five outings have all been outside the frame.

runners_data.name: Yaaser
runners_data.note: Jim Goldie's eight-year-old returns just two days after last running, which is an unusually quick turnaround and deserves monitoring; form shows multiple placed efforts over 7-8f on good ground but winning form is absent, and being shuffled into a midfield slot away from their preferred hold-up berth blunts what finishing burst they possess.
runners_data.comment: Yaaser is winless in his last six starts and was beaten into eighth last time out just two days ago, leaving fitness and form both questionable; he has run over today's trip and going, and stall one is his draw, but the trainer's current 4% strike rate offers little encouragement.

runners_data.name: Catton Lady
runners_data.note: Top-weighted at 142lbs and has placed four times from five recent runs showing genuine consistency; naturally a hold-up type who has run well over 8f on good and soft, and the drop to 7f at Ayr is worth watching as she may be held up and left needing a quicker pace than this race is likely to produce.
runners_data.comment: Catton Lady has finished second twice in her last five starts and steps up as a leading contender here, with experience of today's trip and going working in her favour from stall five at 142 lb. Winless in that recent spell, consistency is the slight concern.

runners_data.name: Gressington
runners_data.note: Katie Scott's five-year-old has been running on good ground all season with best recent effort a fourth over 8f; headgear (b) is worn again and form figures of 7-4-7-10-8 suggest this is a horse that finds a way to finish in the midfield pack without quite getting competitive — the race shape does nothing to change that prognosis.
runners_data.comment: Gressington carries a useful 7 lb pull over his official mark and rates the one to beat on our figures, having run over today's trip and going before; winless in his last six starts, he'll need to find improvement, but 19 days between runs leaves him fresh enough to deliver it from stall 12.

runners_data.name: Pal Joey
runners_data.note: Headgear (t) is a notable flag for Ben Haslam's four-year-old, who has recent experience at shorter trips over 5-6f on varied ground; stepping back up to 7f on good at Ayr after a series of modest efforts, including one win on good over 5f, means the trip looks their outer limit and they will need significant improvement to factor.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last six starts, with an eighth last time out and a fifth three starts back representing his better recent efforts, Pal Joey faces an uphill task from stall nine carrying 140 lb off an official mark of 63, though the experience over today's trip and going at least removes one unknown.

runners_data.name: Kelpie Grey
runners_data.note: The race-shaper for Goldie — raced just two days ago which is a quick turnaround but connections are clearly bullish; all five recent runs have been over 6f and this step up to 7f is unproven, which represents a genuine question mark over whether they can sustain the pace they are likely to set all the way to the line, and headgear is not worn, suggesting a natural front-running tendency.
runners_data.comment: Kelpie Grey has run over today's trip and going, and his rating of 67 gives him solid claims at this level from stall two; yet winless in his last six starts and back just two days ago with a struggling trainer, he needs to find significant improvement.

races.paceDynamic: Kelpie Grey is the lone confirmed front-runner in this 13-runner 7f handicap and, with no genuine challenger to their lead, Paul Mulrennan can dictate a sustainable, controlled gallop from the front — this is not a race where pace will be manufactured by competing leaders. The field is overwhelmingly populated by hold-up and midfield types, meaning the pace is unlikely to be truly searching, and horses racing close to Kelpie Grey will enjoy a significant positional advantage in a race where the tempo may only lift in the final two furlongs. Keep Me Stable is the one runner with genuine prominent credentials and will be expected to sit just off the leader, forming a small lead group. Several genuine hold-up horses — Black Rock Beauty, Novak, Stoneywell, Albeyours, Tropez Power, Yaaser, Joshuas Dream and others — are redistibuted into midfield on the map because the field contains more hold-up types than can all race at the rear, meaning their true position will be further back than ideal and their task is harder than the map implies. The race shape strongly favours horses tracking the pace from a prominent position, as the moderate gallop set by a lone front-runner will likely reward those closest to the action entering the straight rather than closers needing a strong pace to reel in the field.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Kelpie Grey Controls Cleanly
scenarios.trigger: If Kelpie Grey is allowed a soft lead and the gallop remains controlled throughout the seven furlongs, rewarding prominent trackers.
scenarios.body: Kelpie Grey sets a comfortable tempo and nothing applies pressure, meaning the race is run at a pace that suits the leader and any horse sitting just off them; prominent types who travel within striking distance of the front benefit most as the race only quickens late.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Tracker Pounces
scenarios.trigger: If a horse sitting second or third off the steady pace travels well throughout and picks up decisively when the race quickens in the final two furlongs.
scenarios.body: The controlled gallop means horses with a prominent style conserve energy early and arrive at the business end full of running; those with a credible turn of foot from second or third position have the clearest route to victory.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Midfield Finisher Gets Through
scenarios.trigger: If the pace quickens sufficiently in the straight to string the field out and open a gap for a horse finishing from off the pace.
scenarios.body: A genuine surge from Kelpie Grey or Keep Me Stable in the final quarter-mile would create enough of a test to allow a midfield runner with late energy to come through tired horses; Black Rock Beauty, a genuine hold-up type forced forward on this map, would benefit most if able to reclaim closer to their natural hunting ground.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Tearaway Leader Sustains
scenarios.trigger: If Kelpie Grey, freed from any pressure, builds such a comfortable lead that they simply outstay the field and the prominent trackers cannot close the gap in time.
scenarios.body: With no rival to pressure them, Kelpie Grey could steal enough ground early that the final-furlong rally from behind falls marginally short; this scenario is rare on good ground over 7f with a full field but is possible given the complete absence of pace rivals.

watchPoints.text: Kelpie Grey's stamina for 7f is unproven — all five recent runs are over 6f, and if they fade inside the final furlong after controlling the pace, the entire race shape shifts dramatically in favour of prominent trackers.

The unusually quick turnaround for Yaaser (2 days since last run) is worth monitoring in the paddock — any signs of fatigue or sweatiness could indicate this runner is below peak condition and should be discounted further.

Black Rock Beauty's course-and-distance win for Fahey is the standout recent form angle in the race, but their hold-up style is compromised by redistribution — watch whether Oisin Orr attempts to ride closer to the pace than usual or sits and waits, as that tactical decision will define their chance.

Keep Me Stable is the only confirmed prominent type with a realistic chance of sitting directly behind Kelpie Grey; Tom Kiely-Marshall (5lb claim) gives a weight advantage, and Linda Perratt's T14 record of 5/13 suggests a yard in sharp form — their position in the race throughout the early furlongs is the key tactical indicator to follow.

Catton Lady carries top weight of 142lbs and has strong each-way form, but watch whether Joanna Mason opts to push forward earlier than usual given the lack of genuine pace in the race — if she secures a mid-division spot rather than settling at the rear, her chance improves meaningfully.

races.name: Ladbrokes 'Get More With Ladbucks' Handicap Stakes (GBBPlus Race)

runners_data.name: Northwest Passage
runners_data.note: Likely leads by default given no other confirmed front-runner; Jason Hart for Ivan Furtado, 36 days since last run, and the STYLE_FIT flag suggests this is his natural zone but his form at 12f on Good is thin — sim-going record of 0W2P and a wide-trip profile means his lead may be vulnerable late.
runners_data.comment: Yet to win in his last five starts, Northwest Passage nonetheless brings a second two starts back to recommend him, and has run over today's trip and going before; 36 days between runs is a minor query, though his rating of 90 suggests he retains ability.

runners_data.name: Spirit Of Acklam
runners_data.note: Two wins from 13 runs on Good for the Easterby yard, last seen winning over 13f, and headgear (p) adds a focus angle; genuine hold-up horse who will travel from the rear, and Joanna Mason will need a clear run off what may be a compressed pace.
runners_data.comment: Spirit Of Acklam arrives on the back of a win last time out and boasts two victories in his last five starts, with experience over today's trip and conditions working in his favour; the main risk is whether 142 lb from stall nine proves too stiff a burden.

runners_data.name: Star Cast
runners_data.note: Excellent recent form — four wins from last six including on Good ground — and a Prominent profile suits this shape perfectly; Jake Dickson (5lb claim) for Gemma Tutty, who has three winners from 17 in 14 days, and a sim-going return of 1W2P from two runs on Good gives encouragement.
runners_data.comment: Star Cast brings strong recent form — four wins in her last six starts, including back-to-back victories — and has experience of today's trip and conditions; however, 52 days off the track and a hefty 142 lb to carry are the checks against her here.

runners_data.name: Regalian
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse whose last five runs have all been over shorter than today's 1m2f, mainly 8f, on Standard or Soft; headgear (b), Tony Coyle/Kaine Wood trainer with zero wins from six in 14 days, and a 0W3P sim-going record does not inspire confidence at this trip on Good.
runners_data.comment: Regalian showed his best recently with a third four starts back, but has been out of the picture since; however, he returns in good time on 16 days' rest, has run over today's trip and going, and our rating of 92 makes him a serious threat — the risk is his winless recent run.

runners_data.name: Obito
runners_data.note: True hold-up performer with the strongest Good-ground profile in the field — 13 of his last 15 runs on similar going, 2W7P — and David Tudhope is an astute judge of pace; headgear (h) for a horse who was second over 9f on Good and will need a genuinely run race to unleash his best.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last five starts, Obito nevertheless shaped with promise when a second three starts back, and he returns after 32 days with experience of today's trip and going — our rating of 94 makes him the one to beat from stall 4.

runners_data.name: Mano Chicago
runners_data.note: Consistent placing performer, four times runner-up from nine runs on similar going without a win, and headgear (b) for Iain Jardine; a natural hold-up type who will require a contested tempo to close into, and the 49-day absence is a mild query though his Good-ground form is solid.
runners_data.comment: Mano Chicago has been placed second three times in his last five starts and has run over today's trip and going, making him a strong threat at a rating of 93 — though he remains yet to win in recent starts, and 49 days off the track is the query.

runners_data.name: Break The Bank
runners_data.note: Strong placed record on Good ground (3 from recent runs) and connections at Tim Easterby's powerful yard — 4W from 65 in 14 days — make this one interesting; though a natural hold-up horse, he has been redistributed into a midfield slot, and David Allan will have to manage his run carefully given the congestion behind the pace.

runners_data.name: Pearl Eye
runners_data.note: Excellent Good-ground form — 12 of last 15 runs on similar going with 2W4P — and headgear (p) for Jim Goldie; a true hold-up horse shuffled into a midfield mapping position, he ran 14 days ago and the freshness concern is minor; Paul Mulrennan will look to exploit any gaps from the quarter-mile.
runners_data.comment: Fourth last time out blunts his recent claims, though a winner two starts back gives him some hope; he has run over today's trip and going, but the trainer's poor recent strike rate and a stiff 138 lb make it hard to be confident.

runners_data.name: Simply Ruby
runners_data.note: Won over 12f on Soft and has placed over 12-13f, so the trip is right; a natural hold-up horse positioned forward on the map because of redistribution, and with 0W0P on similar going the Dianne Sayer yard (0 from 0 in 14 days) and William Pyle partnership will need a career-best effort.
runners_data.comment: A third three starts back and a winner four starts back show Simply Ruby has ability, but her last two runs have been modest sixth and seventh-place finishes; she has experience over today's trip and going, and 28 days since her last start leaves fitness an open question.

runners_data.name: Cisco Disco
runners_data.note: Eight-year-old Prominent type whose one win came over 10f on Heavier ground; recent form reads 8-7-10-6-1 (win on Heavier) and his sim-going record of 1W1P from 15 runs on Good is weak — Sean Kirrane will push to track the pace but the age and form trajectory are concerns.
runners_data.comment: Landed a winner five starts back but has returned figures of eighth, seventh, unplaced and sixth since, leaving his current form in question; he has experience over today's trip and going, and a 21-day break could freshen him, though the weight of 133 lb is no help.

runners_data.name: Lorca's Waltz
runners_data.note: Three-year-old from William Haggas, who has eight winners from 52 in 14 days — a powerful angle — and Cieren Fallon is an astute booking; a natural hold-up type redistributed into midfield, her Good-ground form is limited (2 runs) but she won over 8f on Good and the step to 10f for Haggas is worth respecting.
runners_data.comment: Lorca's Waltz was a winner two starts back but has finished fifth on his latest start, and ranked last on our figures with 132 lb to carry, he is hard to fancy despite going experience and a fresh enough return.

runners_data.name: Molinari
runners_data.note: Nine-year-old Prominent type whose last five runs are all on Standard or Soft surfaces; sim-going record of just 0W1P from 15 attempts on Good is a significant concern, and Billy Garritty for Martin Todhunter (0 from 4 in 14 days) with 16 days since last run — hard to make a case at this stage of his career.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last five starts, with a sixth last time out and an eighth two starts back, Molinari faces an uphill task from stall 3 off a mark of 66; experience over today's trip and going, plus a quick 16-day turnaround, are modest positives at best.

runners_data.name: Boy Named Sioux
runners_data.note: Three-year-old hold-up type whose entire form base is over 6-7f on Standard — today's 1m2f on Good is a very different proposition; redistributed into midfield, Shane Gray for Fahey (3W from 32 in 14 days) and a win over 7f Tapeta suggests talent, but the trip and going combination is unproven.
runners_data.comment: Consistently finishing mid-pack to rearward in his last five starts — sixth or worse twice, and his sole recent win four starts back — Boy Named Sioux is hard to fancy ranked 11th of 13 on our figures, though he has going experience to call on.

runners_data.name: Ziata
runners_data.note: Won over 10f on Good last time, placed on Soft and Standard, and a Prominent profile suits this race shape directly; Kaiya Fraser for Gemma Tutty (who also saddles Star Cast), 14 days since last run, and a sim-going return of 1W2P from six runs — a live player if she can track the pace and quicken in the straight.
runners_data.comment: Ranked 12 of 13 on our figures, Ziata faces a stiff task against this field, and her speed rating of 66 gives little encouragement; she has run over today's trip and going before, however, and a win last time out at least brings her to the mark in form.

races.paceDynamic: Northwest Passage is the lone confirmed front-runner in a 14-runner field and, with no genuine challenger for the lead, Jason Hart can dictate a controlled, sustainable gallop from the front over this 1m2f Ayr flat. Star Cast, Cisco Disco, Molinari and Ziata will push forward to claim prominent positions just off the leader, creating an orderly pace rather than a contested stampede. The field holds significantly more hold-up types than can realistically settle at the rear — Lorca's Waltz, Pearl Eye, Break The Bank, Simply Ruby, Boy Named Sioux and Mano Chicago are all natural off-the-pace horses, and with so many seeking the same ground, several will inevitably be pushed into mid-division positions that are not their first choice. This race shape — a lone front-runner setting a measured, uncontested pace — most favours horses racing prominently or in the first half of the field who can track the tempo and pounce in the straight, rather than true closers who will need the pace to collapse sufficiently to allow a late run.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Controlled Lead, Prominent Pounce
scenarios.trigger: If Northwest Passage sets an unchallenged, even gallop and the race develops steadily enough for prominent trackers to kick past in the final two furlongs.
scenarios.body: Northwest Passage dictates from the front at a sustainable pace, with Star Cast and Ziata sitting just behind and having enough left in the tank to collar him late; on Good ground at Ayr this scenario rewards horses that race forward and respond to a turning drive.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Pace Collapses, Late Surge
scenarios.trigger: If Northwest Passage goes too fast too soon and the prominent horses get sucked into chasing, leaving a genuine gap for hold-up horses to close.
scenarios.body: A quicker-than-expected early tempo drains the leaders in the final furlong, and horses that have been travelling kindly in mid-division get a clean run to the line; Obito and Mano Chicago, who are genuine form horses on Good ground, are best placed to capitalise from that position.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Fliers Deliver
scenarios.trigger: If the redistribution resolves cleanly and one of the true hold-up types manages to find their natural position with a clear passage through.
scenarios.body: Lorca's Waltz, handled by Cieren Fallon for the powerful William Haggas yard who have eight winners from 52 in the last 14 days, is the most dangerous of the displaced hold-up horses if she gets daylight approaching the final quarter-mile; Pearl Eye's strong Good-ground record also makes her a threat if the front end weakens.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Front-Runner Holds On
scenarios.trigger: If the gallop is slow enough that Northwest Passage simply never gets headed and the prominent trackers fail to find the necessary turn of foot.
scenarios.body: On a flat track with no stiff finish and a compressed field unable to build sustained momentum, a horse that has controlled every aspect of the race from the start can simply outstay rivals lacking a decisive change of pace; Northwest Passage's Prominent profile and fair course form make this a live if secondary possibility.

watchPoints.text: Northwest Passage (J: Jason Hart) is the sole confirmed front-runner — if he is allowed to build an uncontested lead through the first half-mile at a slow pace, those tracking him in prominent positions may simply lack the room to pass him in the straight before hold-up horses can close.

The six redistributed hold-up horses (Lorca's Waltz, Pearl Eye, Break The Bank, Simply Ruby, Boy Named Sioux, Mano Chicago) will all be hunting clear ground at roughly the same point in the straight — watch for a significant traffic scenario that could trap multiple fancied runners behind the pack.

Lorca's Waltz (Cieren Fallon / William Haggas) represents the highest-class trainer angle in the field and, if Fallon elects to push forward rather than settle at the back given the congested hold-up contingent, she could outrun her redistribution mapping and arrive earlier than expected.

Obito (Daniel Tudhope) holds the best quantified Good-ground profile in the race (13/15 runs on similar going, 2W7P) — if the pace does collapse in the final quarter-mile, Tudhope's experience of reading a developing race makes this one worth tracking from the rear of the midfield group.

Gemma Tutty saddles both Star Cast and Ziata — both Prominent types on a favourable going report — and with three winners from 17 in 14 days the trainer is in form; if both horses push forward to track Northwest Passage, their combined presence could determine the entire shape of the final two furlongs.

races.name: Ladbrokes 'Insure Your Acca On Football' Handicap Stakes

runners_data.name: Velvet Skies
runners_data.note: Mapped to the lead as the sole confirmed pacemaker; a natural hold-up type racing entirely out of role, which tempers confidence, but her tactical position is unrivalled — no one else is likely to challenge for the front, and her Good-ground record over 5-7f shows she is not without ability in these conditions.
runners_data.comment: Velvet Skies ran second last time out and has experience of today's trip and conditions, making him a clear danger at the weights; the risk is that he's been winless in his last six starts, suggesting a win remains elusive.

runners_data.name: Water Of Leith
runners_data.note: Eight-year-old hold-up sprinter for Jim Goldie who was out just two days ago; best form is at 5f rather than 6f on Good, and her Good-ground record of 6 runs without a win and only one placed effort is a clear concern at this trip.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last six starts and unplaced just two days ago, Water Of Leith arrives with minimal recovery time and a trainer firing at just 4% recently; he has run over today's trip and going before, but carrying 138 lb from stall 13 leaves plenty to overcome.

runners_data.name: Henery Hawk
runners_data.note: Linda Perratt veteran with three placed efforts from four runs on Good ground; races from the rear but his 5f and 6f form on Good is genuinely consistent, and David Allan's positive record at Ayr makes this a live runner if he can find a prominent enough berth at the foot of the field.
runners_data.comment: Henery Hawk has placed third twice in his last three starts and has run over today's trip and going, yet that fifth two starts back and an unplaced run in recent form suggest consistency is the issue; 135 lb from stall six makes life no easier.

runners_data.name: Edmond Halley
runners_data.note: Cian Horgan (5) takes the ride for Edward Bethell, a yard in good form (T14: 7/29); no wins or placed runs in three Good-ground starts and all recent form has been at 5f, so the step back to 6f on Good is a dual question mark.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last five starts, Edmond Halley at least steps back up to a trip and going he has experience of, and 26 days between runs suggests he arrives fresh; yet rated 57 officially and ranked ninth of 15 on our assessment, he faces a stiff ask from the midfield draw.

runners_data.name: Head For Freedom
runners_data.note: Joanna Mason partners this 3yo for Easterby; the horse has a win and two placed efforts from six Good-ground starts over 6f and is 57 days off a run, but the fitness angle is offset by genuine form at this trip and on this going — a hold-up type who has raced prominently when conditions allowed.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last five starts, Head For Freedom nonetheless catches the eye on a our rating of 70 — top of the fifteen, if only narrowly — and he has run over today's distance and going before. Two encouraging fourth-place finishes in recent starts suggest capability, though consistency remains elusive.

runners_data.name: Lord Abama
runners_data.note: Michael Dods runner with a blinker; a genuine hold-up type nudged into a midfield mapping because the rear is oversubscribed — his ten Good-ground appearances have yielded one win and three placed efforts and this represents his best going, though Sean Kirrane will need to find a clear run.
runners_data.comment: Lord Abama heads the dangers on our ratings despite being winless in his last six starts — he's fit from a run nine days ago, has experience over today's trip and going, and our rating of 68 puts him right in contention; the risk is that recent form has been patchy.

runners_data.name: Macedonian
runners_data.note: Visor-equipped 4yo for Michael Dods, true hold-up racer shifted to midfield on the map because there is no room at the rear; all five recent runs have been at 7f, and returning to 6f on Good where he has one place from six visits is a legitimate concern.
runners_data.comment: Macedonian has run over today's trip and going before, and a speed rating of 72 gives him strong claims as a genuine danger at a mark of 55 — the concern is that he has been winless in his last five starts, with finishes no better than seventh in that sequence.

runners_data.name: White Umbrella
runners_data.note: Blinkered hold-up type for Christopher Kellett; T14 record of 0 from 4 is the weakest trainer strike-rate in the field, and his three Good-ground runs at 6-7f have returned no placing — Tom Eaves picks up the ride but the numbers are against him.
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last six starts, White Umbrella at least has experience over today's trip and going, and 11 days since her last run suggests she arrives fresh; fourth two starts back offers mild encouragement, though her overall profile from stall two carrying 130 lb makes improvement hard to call.

runners_data.name: Doon The Glen
runners_data.note: Visor-wearing 6yo for Jim Goldie, out just two days ago alongside stablemate Water Of Leith; his Good-ground record is the strongest in the entire field (12 runs, 1 win, 3 placed) and he recently won over 6f on Good — a natural closer who needs luck in running from the rear but must be respected.

runners_data.name: Pivotal Terms
runners_data.note: Hood-wearing 3yo for Iain Jardine (T14: 6/30, a strong in-form yard); four runs on Good ground without a win but two placed efforts at 5f, and being mapped to midfield rather than his natural hold-up position slightly flatters his tactical situation — Andrew Mullen rides.
runners_data.comment: Ran unplaced last time but shaped with promise when second three starts back, and a winner six starts back; she has experience over today's trip and going, and returns quickly enough at 10 days. The 128 lb burden may test her.

runners_data.name: Monastere
runners_data.note: Karl Thornton's 4yo is flagged as fading in the finish and is a genuine hold-up type pushed into a midfield mapping; his Good-ground record shows a win and two places from seven attempts, but the fade flag and the race shape favouring prominently-placed horses are both negatives.
runners_data.comment: Ranked bottom of this field on our figures, Monastere hasn't won in his last two starts — that sole recent victory now three starts back — and draw 15 adds another question mark. He has run over today's distance and going before, and 24 days between runs suggests he's fresh.

runners_data.name: Sixcor
runners_data.note: Pads-wearing hold-up specialist for Linda Perratt; has a 6f Good-ground win on her record and four placed efforts from ten Good-ground starts — among the most consistent closers in the field, and Tom Kiely-Marshall (5) should allow her to be covered up and produced late if the pace is strong enough.
runners_data.comment: Sixcor was a winner two starts back but has disappointed since, finishing fourth last time out, and ranked 11th of 15 on our figures he faces a stiff ask here. Has run over today's trip and going, and ten days between runs suggests he's ready.

runners_data.name: Ski Angel
runners_data.note: Amie Waugh (3) rides for R Mike Smith (T14: 1/16); a natural hold-up type repositioned to midfield, with one placed effort from ten Good-ground starts — the form reads as consistently placed just outside the money rather than a winning threat in a race of this shape.
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last six starts, with a seventh last time out and an eighth two starts back, Ski Angel faces a stiff ask from stall 12 off an official mark of 45, though she has run over today's trip and going before and returns on a reasonable 14-day turnaround.

runners_data.name: Red Walls
runners_data.note: Jack Nicholls (3) rides this 8yo for Lisa Williamson; all five recent runs have been on Standard ground and her sole placing on Good was third over 6f on the all-weather equivalent — switching to turf Good is an unknown and the form profile is not encouraging.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last five starts, with three eighths among the recent figures, Red Walls is hard to fancy at the foot of the rankings here; he has run over today's trip and going before, and a third two starts back offers a sliver of hope.

runners_data.name: Baby Rover
runners_data.note: Greg Fairley partners Katie Scott's 4yo; has a win and three places from nine Good-ground starts at 6f, making this a competitive profile for the conditions — a natural hold-up type shifted to midfield, but the genuine form on Good at this trip makes him a player if he can find a clear passage.
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last six starts and ranked 13th of 15 on our figures, Baby Rover faces a stiff ask here; a third last time out offers slim encouragement, though she has run over today's trip and going before.

runners_data.name: Lanarra
runners_data.note: William Pyle rides the R Mike Smith 3yo, who raced just two days ago; her record shows no wins but two placed efforts from seven Good-ground starts at 6-7f, and consistent second and third placings at this trip suggest she stays competitive without quite winning — a hold-up type who needs the pace to materialise.

races.paceDynamic: Velvet Skies is the sole confirmed front-runner in this 16-runner 6f handicap on Good ground at Ayr, and with no genuine rival to push her through the early furlongs, she is likely to control proceedings at a comfortable, sustainable tempo from the front. The bulk of this field — Macedonian, Lord Abama, Pivotal Terms, Doon The Glen, Sixcor, Baby Rover and others — are true hold-up or prominent types who have been redistributed on the map because there is simply nowhere near enough natural pace or prominent racing room for all of them; in practice, several will be forced to race closer than their habits suggest, creating mid-race congestion rather than a true end-to-end gallop. On Good ground over 6f at Ayr, a leader controlling a muddling pace is a significant tactical advantage, and the horses best placed to exploit it are those able to travel prominently or just off the pace without covering excess ground — genuine closer form in this field may be compromised by a tempo that never truly stretches. The race shape strongly favours a prominent racer or a horse capable of producing a clean, well-timed run from just off the leader, as the field of hold-up types will face a wall of traffic and a pace that may simply not be strong enough to bring them into the race late.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Velvet Skies Dictates Alone
scenarios.trigger: If Velvet Skies crosses cleanly, sets a comfortable gallop and is never headed, the tempo remains controlled and she runs out a clear winner.
scenarios.body: Velvet Skies, although a natural hold-up type redistributed to the front, has the best tactical position in a race with no other confirmed pacesetter, and on Good ground at Ayr's flat 6f track she can control the race from the front without burning out. A steady tempo punishes the field of hold-up horses who need a true gallop to produce their finishing kick, leaving those who track her as the main beneficiaries.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Stalker Pounces
scenarios.trigger: If a horse settles in second or third behind Velvet Skies and produces a clean, well-timed challenge entering the final furlong.
scenarios.body: With the pace controlled by Velvet Skies, the horse who tracks her at a length or two has the ideal position and the rail to run against, and on Good ground the winner in this scenario comes from just off the pace rather than deep in the field. Horses like Head For Freedom, Henery Hawk and Baby Rover have the right profile — all have demonstrated ability to race prominently and finish strongly at this trip on Good.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Closers Charge Through
scenarios.trigger: If the early pace is quicker than expected, stringing out the field and producing a true test that brings hold-up types into the race late.
scenarios.body: In this scenario genuine hold-up horses such as Doon The Glen, Sixcor and Lanarra, who have the strongest Good-ground profiles in the field, benefit from a stronger gallop that plays to their finishing ability. However this shape is penalised by the reality that most of this field are also natural closers who are unlikely to generate the required pace, making it the least likely outcome for a clean sweep from the rear.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Pace Collapse, Field Bunches
scenarios.trigger: If Velvet Skies sets an extremely dawdling pace that causes the field to bunch and the race is decided by a sprint in the final two furlongs.
scenarios.body: A very slow early gallop compresses the field into a tight group, making draw and wider tactical positioning critical, and horses with a sharp early turn of foot such as Pivotal Terms or Monastere could capitalise in a sprint-finish scramble. This scenario is the least predictable and most volatile, as a 16-runner bunched sprint on Good ground is high-risk for everyone regardless of profile.

watchPoints.text: Doon The Glen ran just two days ago and comes out of the same Jim Goldie yard as Water Of Leith — monitor the market early for any stable money, as his Good-ground form over 6f is comfortably the strongest in the field and a fit, in-form closer of this profile can be dangerous even from the rear in a race that may not have a true gallop.

Head For Freedom has been off 57 days and Joanna Mason must judge pace perfectly behind a lone front-runner — if she can slot into second or third early, this 3yo's form on Good over 6f gives her a live chance and she is the most likely horse to pounce on Velvet Skies inside the final furlong.

With 16 horses, the majority mapped to midfield or hold-up positions, early draw and positioning will be critical — watch for any horses drawn wide (high numbers) who are forced to cover extra ground in a race where the pace is unlikely to be strong enough to reward a wide, late run.

Sixcor's trainer Linda Perratt has a T14 strike-rate of 5/13, one of the strongest in the race, and the yard also saddles Henery Hawk — if both are fancied in the market it suggests Perratt has this race targeted, and Sixcor's Good-ground form over 5f may be exposed over the extra furlong.

Macedonian and Lord Abama are both Michael Dods hold-up types with headgear; should both jockeys (Mark Winn and Sean Kirrane) attempt to track Velvet Skies closer than their natural style, there is a risk of overcrowding behind the leader in the early stages, which could disrupt several of the midfield runners simultaneously.

runners_data.note: Wilf Storey's 5yo is a genuine hold-up horse by nature but is mapped into midfield because the rear of the field is simply oversubscribed — Paula Muir claims 3lb and may be able to find a clear position, but Good ground form is thin (one win from five similar-going runs) and the style-fit discount applies.
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last five starts, Idyllic does bring distance and going experience to this assignment, and 16 days between runs suggests she arrives fresh; the concern is a consistent pattern of unplaced or mid-division finishes that makes improvement hard to pin on.
