runners_data.note: Jim Goldie's yard has been in productive form (2/51 over 14 days is modest but active) and this 6yo has shown ability on Good ground over 10f, placed three times in that scenario; the hold-up style means she needs gaps to appear and the straight to suit, which is plausible on flat Ayr.
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last six starts with a record that reads 3rd, 4th, 5th, 8th, 9th, 7th in recent outings, Penelope's Sister faces a stiff task ranked tenth of twelve, and a trainer striking at just 4% compounds the concern — experience over today's trip and going is the one genuine consolation.

runners_data.name: Ravenscraig Castle
runners_data.note: Iain Jardine has been in strong 14-day form (6/30) and this 8yo veteran has placed at 16f on Good going, showing he stays well and handles this course; fitted with blinkers, he is likely to race prominently and is very well-placed tactically to track Positive Thoughts from early.
runners_data.comment: Ravenscraig Castle arrives here on the back of a fourth last time out and has run over today's trip and going, while our rating of 70 marks him out as a serious threat to the top-rated runner; the concern is he's winless in his last five starts.

runners_data.name: Recobella
runners_data.note: Philip Kirby's mare has won on Good ground over 10f and placed three times at 12f — the trip is right and the going suits — but her natural position at the back of the field has been nudged into midfield mapping because of the hold-up traffic, meaning her actual chance is somewhat discounted by the race shape.
runners_data.comment: Ranked bottom-two on our figures and rated well below the field's upper end, Recobella is hard to fancy despite winning last time out; she has run over today's trip and going, and her draw of 2 at least keeps things simple from the gate.

runners_data.name: Lightning Galaxy
runners_data.note: Michael Dods runner whose best form has come on Good going but almost always in sprint trips of 6-8f; now stepping up to 10f on turf for the first time in this company, the style-fit issue compounds a distance concern and recent form figures of 9959 are deeply uninspiring.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last five starts, with three ninths among them, Lightning Galaxy has a poor recent profile to overcome; he has run over today's going before and returns after 35 days, but carrying 132 lb from stall 11, there is little in the figures to suggest a turnaround.

runners_data.name: She's Got Bottle
runners_data.note: Lizzie Quinlan's 7yo returns after a 297-day absence — that is the most significant flag in this field — and despite being a true hold-up runner forced into a midfield mapping, the layoff alone makes it very hard to trust even if the trip (10f on Good) is not obviously wrong.
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last five starts and absent for 297 days, She's Got Bottle does at least have experience over today's distance and going, and a rating of 66 suggests she holds more ability than her official mark of 55 implies — the fitness question after that lengthy layoff is the obvious concern.

runners_data.name: Positive Thoughts
runners_data.note: Jason Hart takes the ride on John & Sean Quinn's 3yo, the only confirmed front-runner in the race; blinkers fitted and lightly weighted at 128lbs, the horse has some Good-ground form and should lead without challenge, making it the single most influential horse in dictating the shape of this contest.
runners_data.comment: Positive Thoughts has been winless in her last five starts, with a third two runs back the lone bright spot in a largely disappointing recent sequence; she has run over today's going before, but ranked ninth of twelve on our figures, she faces a stiff ask here.

runners_data.name: Parole Officer
runners_data.note: Ewan Whillans yard has been active (3/13 over 14 days) and this 3yo has shown ability at 10f, with headgear notes (p) suggesting some quirks; a true hold-up runner forced into midfield mapping, and form figures of 54-990 offer little confidence that it can improve enough to get involved.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last five starts, Parole Officer has at least run over today's trip and going before, though his recent string of unplaced efforts — including back-to-back ninths — give little encouragement; the 35-day break and a rating of 62 suggest there may be more to offer, but he faces a stiff ask from stall 8.

races.paceDynamic: Positive Thoughts is the sole confirmed front-runner in this 12-runner 1m2f handicap and, with no genuine challenger to the lead from the rest of the field, Jason Hart should be able to dictate a controlled, even tempo on Good ground without any serious pressure applied. The pace map is congested behind the leader — Naturalia and Ravenscraig Castle are the most likely prominent horses to track Positive Thoughts, while the bulk of the field clusters in midfield and beyond. Several runners including Idyllic, Recobella, She's Got Bottle, Lightning Galaxy, Parole Officer, and Lesrico are true hold-up types whose natural positions at the rear have been mapped to midfield simply because the field contains more horses wanting to settle off the pace than the race shape can physically accommodate at the back. With a single unhurried pace-setter setting a sustainable gallop and a flat track at Ayr over a distance that rewards stamina alongside finishing kick, this race shape most strongly favours horses racing prominently or in a handy mid-division berth who can travel comfortably and sustain their effort into the straight, rather than deep closers who depend on a strong pace and a true test of late stamina.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Positive Thoughts Controls Wire-To-Wire
scenarios.trigger: If Positive Thoughts secures an uncontested lead and Jason Hart controls the tempo to set up a sprint finish from the front.
scenarios.body: Hart dictates a measured pace without pressure, keeps Positive Thoughts fresh, and the 3yo front-runner simply has too much petrol left when the field comes to challenge in the straight on this flat Ayr track. Prominent runners like Naturalia and Ravenscraig Castle who track the leader are best placed to capitalise if the leader tires, but the lack of pace pressure makes a front-runner's day.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Stalkers Reel In Leader
scenarios.trigger: If Positive Thoughts sets a slightly quicker-than-comfortable pace and the tracking horses Naturalia or Ravenscraig Castle time their challenge perfectly in the straight.
scenarios.body: Naturalia has repeatedly placed over this trip and goes well on Good ground, while Ravenscraig Castle has shown he handles this course and trip combination; either horse tracking the pace closely is ideally positioned to pounce once the front-runner reaches the limit of stamina. Paul Mulrennan on Naturalia and Cara Tuke on Ravenscraig Castle both have horses with the right profile to capitalise on a genuine finish.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horse Storms Through
scenarios.trigger: If the pace collapses in the home straight and a truly held-up finisher finds a clear run to produce a strong late challenge.
scenarios.body: This scenario depends on horses like Recobella or Lesrico — genuine deep closers — being able to work through traffic and hit the line hard, which is less likely when their natural positions at the rear have been crowded out by the field's excess of hold-up types. Recobella does have a winning profile on Good ground and at this sort of trip, but the expectation of a modest, controlled tempo makes it hard to generate the pace collapse this shape requires.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Chaotic Mid-Race Scramble
scenarios.trigger: If several jockeys push forward aggressively off the break to challenge Positive Thoughts, creating an unexpectedly contested pace that burns off the whole field.
scenarios.body: Should pace pressure materialise and the race turn frenetic mid-race, every frontrunner and prominent horse could tie up in the straight and leave a late-finisher with a rare clear passage — but given this field's redistribution problem, the true hold-up types are not even getting their preferred rear position, so capitalising on a pace collapse remains genuinely difficult. The most likely beneficiary in this unlikely scenario would be whichever horse manages to get widest and latest into the straight.

watchPoints.text: Positive Thoughts (Jason Hart) — if Hart is able to slot in at the front unchallenged, the lack of any pace rival means the tempo is entirely in his hands; watch whether he allows the field to close or kicks clear early, as that single decision shapes every other scenario.

Ravenscraig Castle — Iain Jardine's yard is in strong form and this blinker-fitted prominent type is one of the few horses naturally placed to track the leader; if he travels smoothly two lengths off the pace into the straight, he becomes the most dangerous challenger to Positive Thoughts.

Naturalia — with four recent placed efforts at this sort of trip and Paul Mulrennan booked, this is the horse best suited to capitalise if Positive Thoughts sets a comfortable gallop and the prominent position becomes the winning one; monitor market moves given consistent recent form.

She's Got Bottle — a 297-day absence is the single longest layoff in the field and should be noted as a significant reliability risk regardless of how the race is run; Barry McHugh may need to nurse her through the race if she is rusty, and any drift in the market would confirm trainer expectations are modest.

Lightning Galaxy — stepping up markedly in trip from 6-8f sprints to 10f on turf for the first time in this company, the distance question is real and should temper any interest generated by the name or the Michael Dods yard regardless of pace shape.

races.name: Ladbrokes 'Free Rewards With Instant Spins' Handicap Stakes (Div II)

runners_data.name: West Tyrone
runners_data.note: Sole confirmed front-runner, Lizzie Quinlan's 4-year-old carries the headgear flag (hg:p) and returns after 62 days off; if he replicates his OR=65 form and gets an uncontested lead, he is the primary shape-setter for the entire race.
runners_data.comment: West Tyrone shaped well when third last time out and is a placed runner in recent starts, with experience over today's trip and going — our rating ranks him top of the field. The concern is 62 days off and being winless in his last five starts.

runners_data.name: Royal Blaze
runners_data.note: T14 strike rate of 3/13 for Whillans is encouraging, and two recent wins over 10f on good going suggest this 5-year-old is in fine form; naturally a hold-up type but likely to press forward given the lack of genuine pace and has the form to be competitive.
runners_data.comment: Royal Blaze arrives on the back of back-to-back wins and races fresh on 14 days, yet his official rating of 64 and a speed rating just below that suggest he's working at his ceiling, and that ninth three starts back is a reminder he's not entirely reliable.

runners_data.name: Spirit Catcher
runners_data.note: Cieren Fallon takes the mount on this 7-year-old who has placed twice over 12f on good ground recently; a natural closer whose best chance comes if the steady tempo still leaves enough to aim at, though the trip and going suit him well.
runners_data.comment: Spirit Catcher has run over today's trip and going, carries a manageable 139 lb from stall 11, and our rating of 69 marks him out as a leading threat in this field — the concern is a run of three consecutive below-par finishes heading into this.

runners_data.name: Sweet Kiss
runners_data.note: Tim Easterby's 4-year-old is at heart a hold-up performer, but the sheer volume of closers in this field means she will likely find herself racing closer to the pace than ideal — her STYLE_FIT of 0.91 tempers expectations accordingly.
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last five starts, Sweet Kiss nonetheless brings some encouragement — second last time out suggests fitness and form are ticking along, and she has run over today's trip and going before; 137 lb from stall 2 is the main query.

runners_data.name: Tee Aitch Aye
runners_data.note: Iain Jardine's 5-year-old has headgear (hg:p) and a recent third on good ground over 10f, but this horse's natural closing style is compromised by the crowded rear division; a STYLE_FIT of 0.90 reflects the difficulty of getting a clear passage.
runners_data.comment: Tee Aitch Aye shaped with promise when third last time out, and returning after 35 days he has experience of today's distance and going. Winless in recent starts, but that third has him in good heart, and a rating of 69 makes him worth including from stall seven.

runners_data.name: Motawaared
runners_data.note: Jim Goldie's 4-year-old has posted a consistent string of mid-pack finishes and the form figures are uninspiring; naturally inclined to come from behind, but pushed into a midfield mapping given the hold-up congestion, reducing his chance of landing in the right position.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last six starts, with a string of fifth and sixth-place finishes, Motawaared has experience of today's distance and going but the trainer's recent record of 2/51 is a concern, even if the 21-day break offers some hope of a revival from stall one.

runners_data.name: Glasses Up
runners_data.note: Veteran 11-year-old for R Mike Smith, David Allan aboard, who won over 13f on good going in recent form (1/13f/GOO); a habitual hold-up performer who will struggle to express that style fully given the field composition, though his good-ground record and longer-trip form are genuine assets.
runners_data.comment: Ranked 11 of 12 on our figures, Glasses Up has been out of the frame in his last four starts since winning two runs back, and that modest official rating of 57 underlines how hard he is to fancy; he has run over today's trip and going before, which is something.

runners_data.name: Ceinture d'Orion
runners_data.note: Daniel Tudhope is a significant jockey booking for David O'Meara's 3-year-old, whose four-run form reads consistently placed on good ground; likely to get a prominent berth through jockey intent, which would suit the expected race shape well.
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last four starts and ranked tenth of twelve on our figures, Ceinture d'Orion faces a stiff task here; she has experience over today's trip and going, and a third two starts back offers a slender crumb of comfort, but 39 days off and 133 lb from stall nine add further questions.

runners_data.name: Cosmic Man
runners_data.note: Kevin Ryan's 3-year-old carries a ⚠ fade warning and returns after 62 days off; his recent form over shorter trips on soft/standard going doesn't inspire confidence at 1m2f on good ground today, and the finishing concern compounds the risk.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last five starts, with two eighths and a ninth among those efforts, Cosmic Man has been well held in recent starts and our figures rank him near the foot of this field — 62 days off the track adds further doubt, though he has run over today's trip and going before.

runners_data.name: Farabove The Limit
runners_data.note: Phillip Makin's 3-year-old returns from a lengthy 187-day break, which is a major question mark; a natural hold-up type squeezed into a midfield role by field dynamics, and with only 2 from 7 runs on comparable going, the combination of absence and style misfit makes this a tough ask.
runners_data.comment: Ran third three starts back and returned a close fourth last time out, giving Farabove The Limit solid claims on a mark of 60, and experience over today's trip and going helps his case — though 187 days off the track is the clear concern.

runners_data.name: Rugby Union
runners_data.note: Gemma Tutty's 3-year-old carries a ⚠ fade flag alongside a STYLE_FIT of 0.91, and the form string of 9-0595 over 10f on good ground paints a horse that struggles to land a blow; running out of natural position compounds the underlying form concern.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last five starts and ranked last on our figures, Rugby Union faces a stiff ask here; he has run over today's trip and returns on a handy 14-day turnaround, but a career-best is needed to trouble these rivals.

runners_data.name: Onyeisi
runners_data.note: Karl Thornton's 3-year-old wears a hood (hg:b) and has been placed once over 10f on good ground; a genuine hold-up type mapped to midfield due to the congested rear division, but with a STYLE_FIT of 0.93 — the highest redistribution penalty in the field — his chance of racing effectively is most at risk.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last six starts, Onyeisi nonetheless steps back to familiar distance and going conditions and, rated 60 by us against an official mark of 55, there may be a sliver of upside — though his tendency to finish mid-pack or worse makes a bold showing hard to bank on.

races.paceDynamic: West Tyrone is the sole confirmed front-runner in this 12-runner field and, with no genuine pace rival to pressure him, Shane Gray can dictate a measured, sustainable gallop from the front over this 1m2f trip on good ground at Ayr. The rest of the field is dominated by hold-up and midfield types, meaning the pace will almost certainly be controlled and even, with no mid-race surge to unsettle the leader. This race shape heavily favours horses who can travel prominently just off West Tyrone's shoulder and kick early in the straight, rather than those who need a truly run race to deliver a late burst. The field holds significantly more hold-up types than can all settle at the rear — Sweet Kiss, Farabove The Limit, Tee Aitch Aye, Motawaared, Glasses Up, Rugby Union and Onyeisi are all natural closers competing for positions they may not obtain, with Royal Blaze, Spirit Catcher and Ceinture d'Orion most likely to secure a genuine prominent pitch behind the leader.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Controlled Lead, Early Kick
scenarios.trigger: If West Tyrone bowls along in front at a steady pace and the prominent trackers deliver their challenge smoothly entering the straight.
scenarios.body: West Tyrone sets a comfortable, uncontested tempo and those close to him in the early stages are gifted an energy advantage, needing only to overhaul a front-runner who has not been stretched.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Pair Pounce
scenarios.trigger: If West Tyrone's lead is challenged by horses pressing forward off the steady pace, creating a small group that fights it out from the home turn.
scenarios.body: The even gallop encourages several hold-up types to travel closer than normal, compressing the field and producing a blanket finish among the front quartet entering the final two furlongs.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Late Closers Arrive
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is surprisingly honest enough to set up a genuine late run and one of the deeper-lying hold-up horses finds a clear run in the straight.
scenarios.body: A genuine, unimpeded passage would be required, and the redistribution of so many hold-up types into midfield makes this scenario structurally crowded and difficult to execute cleanly.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Front Runner Wires Field
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is genuinely slow and West Tyrone's rider pinches an unchallenged break that the hold-up-heavy field cannot close down in time.
scenarios.body: With the bulk of the field operating out of their natural role and unable to mount a coordinated late challenge, a horse travelling well within himself in front could simply steal the race.

watchPoints.text: West Tyrone's uncontested lead is the race's defining factor — if Shane Gray controls the pace entirely, the race shape is set and all hold-up horses are immediately disadvantaged.

The seven redistributed hold-up types (Sweet Kiss, Tee Aitch Aye, Motawaared, Glasses Up, Farabove The Limit, Rugby Union, Onyeisi) will compress the midfield early, creating significant traffic risk in the straight — watch for horses stuck behind a wall of rivals.

Cosmic Man and Rugby Union both carry stamina fade warnings over this 1m2f trip — if either has drifted into a prominent position through the compressed pace, they could cause interference when stopping in the final furlong.

Ceinture d'Orion's Daniel Tudhope booking is worth noting — a top jockey likely to position aggressively from the outset, which could move this horse closer to the pace than its natural style suggests and into the ideal scenario-A position.

Farabove The Limit's 187-day absence is the longest lay-off in the field by a substantial margin — market drifts or shortening for this runner in the final hour before the off would be a telling signal about stable confidence on its return.

races.name: 'Ladbrokes Play 1-2-Free' Handicap Stakes

runners_data.name: Vega Storm
runners_data.note: Fahey handler in solid 14-day form (3/32), though this 3yo has been competing at 6-7f and now steps to a mile for the first time; a true hold-up runner whose preferred rear position will be hard to find in this congested field, capping its realistic chance of producing best.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last six starts, Vega Storm was fourth two starts back before an unplaced effort three starts back clouds confidence, though he has experience over today's trip and going, and returns after 19 days carrying 129 lb from stall seven.

runners_data.name: Light The Night Up
runners_data.note: Burke is a reliable handler at this level and Sam James takes over, but this horse has finished 4th or 5th in its last four starts and has not won — its natural off-the-pace style is further compromised by a field shape that will push it forward of its comfort zone rather than allow it to settle at the back.
runners_data.comment: Consistent if winless in recent starts, Light The Night Up steps up with experience of today's trip and going, and her rating of 70 marks her as a genuine threat from stall 10; the worry is she's yet to convert that consistency into a win.

runners_data.name: Hatamoto
runners_data.note: Tim Easterby's 3yo has winning form over 8f on good ground and arrives just 14 days after a run, which speaks to fitness; the hood (hg:p) is retained, and despite being a genuine closer, it is the strongest form case among the hold-up brigade and capable of making its presence felt if the pace truly tests the front-runners.
runners_data.comment: Hatamoto won two of his last six starts and returns on a quick 14-day turnaround with experience of today's trip and going in his favour, but that sixth last time out tempers enthusiasm, and he faces stiff competition rated above him from stall six carrying 126 lb.

runners_data.name: Our Randolph
runners_data.note: Prominent racer for Michael Dods who has struggled in recent handicap form (7th, 8th, 9th) but returns after 56 days fresher; the fades-in-finish flag is a notable concern on a mile trip where stamina will be tested, and the Ayr track offers no hiding place.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last three starts, with finishes of ninth, eighth and seventh in recent outings, Our Randolph arrives after a 56-day absence and ranks last on our figures here; he has run over today's trip and going, but there is precious little else to tempt.

runners_data.name: Beckon
runners_data.note: Susan Corbett's charge returns from 117 days off — the significant freshness angle — and its one win came over 8f on Southwell tapeta, though it has placed at that trip on turf; a clean prominent pitch in a genuinely run race is where it holds the most credible claims.
runners_data.comment: Beckon showed ability with a win three starts back and is third last time out, but 117 days off the track is a significant fitness concern, and ranked eighth of ten on our figures she faces a stiff ask here despite having experience over today's trip.

runners_data.name: Wise Crack
runners_data.note: Ran out a winner over 7f on good at Goodwood 19 days ago wearing a visor (retained here), giving it a well-timed prep; a natural hold-up runner with a recent winning confidence boost, though the step to a mile is untested and its best form is at shorter.
runners_data.comment: Wise Crack won last time out and has experience of today's trip and conditions, but a mixed recent record — four unplaced or beaten efforts in his other last four starts — suggests consistency is the concern, and 132 lb is no easy burden.

runners_data.name: Paroda Diva
runners_data.note: Won over 8f on soft and placed on good at the same trip, so the distance and going combination is not a concern; Patrick Neville's filly returns after 68 days and as a genuine hold-up type, needs the pace to be strong enough to bring her into it late — the race shape is potentially favourable.
runners_data.comment: Paroda Diva brings a win and a runner-up finish in her last two starts, showing sharp recent form, and she has experience of today's distance and going. The main concern is a 68-day absence since that placed effort.

runners_data.name: Napolian
runners_data.note: The highest OR (69) in the field alongside Adiada, and boasts a win over 8f on good going — confirmed front-runner partnered by David Tudhope who rides Ayr brilliantly; arrives 13 days after last run suggesting readiness, but must overcome the attritional effect of a pace duel if Keep An Eye On It refuses to yield.
runners_data.comment: Napolian won three starts back and has run over today's trip and going, so conditions hold no fears; the worry is his two most recent efforts have yielded only a fourth and an unplaced run, suggesting he needs to recapture that earlier spark.

runners_data.name: Adiada
runners_data.note: 293 days off the track is a major flag — this Michael Dods hold-up type has placed at 8f on soft and good, but the layoff makes its fitness impossible to assume; Sean Kirrane takes the ride and the horse could be thrown in lightly if fit, but the absence demands caution.
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last three starts and returning after a lengthy 293-day absence, Adiada faces a stiff task here — our rating of 62 ranks her ninth of ten. She has run over today's trip before, and the second two starts back offers a slim crumb of comfort.

runners_data.name: Keep An Eye On It
runners_data.note: Tony Coyle & Kaine Wood's confirmed front-runner returns after 120 days, which is a significant absence for a pace-dependent horse that will need to be fully tuned to compete aggressively for the lead; placed at 8f on good ground, it is capable but must prove freshness is an asset rather than a liability at the business end.
runners_data.comment: Consistent in the places, Keep An Eye On It brings solid each-way form — third last time out, second two starts back — and has experience over today's trip and conditions. Drawing stall one carrying 133 lb, he's yet to win in recent starts but tops our figures.

races.paceDynamic: Napolian and Keep An Eye On It are the two confirmed front-runners in this ten-runner mile handicap on good ground at Ayr, and with both expected to assert early, a genuinely contested gallop from the outset is the most probable outcome — neither has the profile to simply yield to the other. The resulting honest, even tempo over Ayr's flat mile is likely to suit horses who can travel prominently without burning energy in the scramble, particularly those capable of sustaining their effort through the final two furlongs rather than producing a sudden burst. Beckon and Our Randolph are the prominent types best positioned to benefit from sitting just off the pace without having to fight for it, while Wise Crack and Paroda Diva, despite natural hold-up tendencies, carry realistic each-way claims if the gallop is truly strong and the race comes back to them. This field holds considerably more hold-up horses than the rear of the field can accommodate — Vega Storm, Light The Night Up, and Hatamoto are genuine closers but are unlikely to secure their preferred position given the competitive shape, reducing their chance of producing their best; the race shape most clearly favours prominent racers who travel smoothly into the contest without expending early energy.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Contested Lead, Prominent Wins
scenarios.trigger: If Napolian and Keep An Eye On It fight for the front and set an honest gallop that stretches the field throughout.
scenarios.body: The two leaders burn each other up through the early stages, leaving Beckon and Our Randolph to travel smoothly in behind before picking them off in the closing stages; Ayr's flat mile with no bend bias rewards those who settle just off the pace and sustain their run. This is the most likely shape given dual front-runners with no inclination to concede, and prominent types who avoid early traffic are well placed.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Leaders Fade, Closers Land
scenarios.trigger: If the front-runners set a genuinely strong early pace that fully collapses their finishing effort, leaving a gap for resolute hold-up horses.
scenarios.body: Hatamoto, the best-credentialed hold-up horse in the field with two recent wins and solid good-ground form, would be the prime beneficiary if pace truly injures the leaders; Wise Crack's recent Goodwood win and the visor suggest a horse primed for a bold run from the rear on a day when conditions encourage late challengers. The probability is tempered by the redistribution problem — Vega Storm and Light The Night Up are unlikely to get a clean run from their natural position given how congested the rear will be.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Front-Runner Dictates
scenarios.trigger: If one of the two pace horses — most likely Napolian with Tudhope in the saddle — breaks more sharply and quickly establishes a clear lead, forcing Keep An Eye On It to accept a tracking role.
scenarios.body: Napolian, who won over this course-and-distance configuration at 8f on good ground, could exploit a clean break to control tempo, presenting Tudhope — Ayr's most accomplished jockey — with the opportunity to dial down the pace and produce a tactical sprint. If the race is run this way, hold-up types are firmly disadvantaged and the winner comes from the front or just behind it.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Slow Pace, Bunched Finish
scenarios.trigger: If neither front-runner seriously commits early and the field gets away at a dawdle, producing a sprint-style finish.
scenarios.body: A bunched finish over a mile on good ground at Ayr would compress the field and reduce the advantage of pace awareness, theoretically opening the race to Adiada — a long-absent horse whose connections may have her fresh and ready — or Paroda Diva, who has course-and-distance winning form on good ground. This is the least likely shape given two genuine confirmed leaders are declared, but cannot be entirely dismissed.

watchPoints.text: Napolian and Keep An Eye On It — monitor which horse breaks faster and whether one immediately asserts; if Napolian clears immediately under Tudhope, the entire field shape changes from contested to controlled.

Hatamoto — if it fails to find a clear run through a congested rear group given the redistribution of hold-up types, it may never produce its finishing effort despite being the most in-form closer in the field.
Beckon — 117 days off means fitness is unproven; watch for any signs of ring rust in the early stages before treating its prominent position as an asset.

Adiada — 293-day absence makes it a significant unknown; if it shows unexpected freshness in the early part of the race it could be a market mover to monitor, but the layoff is a genuine barrier to blind faith.

Wise Crack — the visor is retained following a recent win and this horse may be sharper than its hold-up tag suggests on form; watch whether Shane Gray opts to ride it more prominently than expected given its recent winning confidence.
